frameworkCheck.title: AP English Literature and Composition Course and Exam Description (effective Fall 2024)
frameworkCheck.how: The CED organizes this course by skills. Each unit's skills were read from the skill column of its unit-overview table in the CED and cross-checked against the Course at a Glance; every skill in a unit is matched to the StudySprint topic whose guide section and questions practice it. Skill wording is the CED's, with spaces restored where the PDF's text runs words together.
frameworkCheck.weightsSource: the CED's exam section, checked 2026-11-09 (weightings are given for each unit type, not for single units)
frameworkCheck.examFormat: From the AP Students assessment page and the CED, checked 2026-11-09: Section 1, 55 multiple-choice questions (45% of the score) in 5 sets of 8–13 questions, each set following a passage of prose fiction (which may include drama) or poetry, with at least 2 prose fiction and 2 poetry passages. Multiple-choice weighting by skill category: character 16–20%, setting 3–6%, plot and structure 16–20%, narrator or speaker 21–26%, word choice, imagery, and symbols 10–13%, comparison 10–13%, textually substantiated arguments 10–13%. Section 2, 3 free-response questions (55%): poetry analysis, prose fiction analysis, and a literary argument about a work the student chooses. StudySprint practice is multiple-choice only, in passage-based sets; essay practice uses College Board's released questions.
differences: The AP Students page's topic lists are summaries in different words from the CED's numbered skills; both are recorded and both are build-checked. Some listed topics (for example, symbolism in Unit 3) go beyond the skills the CED assigns to that unit.

units.name: Unit 1: Short Fiction I
officialTopics: Interpreting the role of character in fiction
Identifying and interpreting setting
Understanding how a story’s structure affects interpretations
Understanding and interpreting a narrator’s perspective
Reading texts literally and figuratively
The basics of literary analysis
units.examWeight: 42–49% (shared by the short fiction units 1, 4, and 7)
frameworkTopics: 1.A Identify and describe what specific textual details reveal about a character, that character’s perspective, and that character’s motives.
2.A Identify and describe specific textual details that convey or reveal a setting.
3.A Identify and describe how plot orders events in a narrative.
3.B Explain the function of a particular sequence of events in a plot.
4.A Identify and describe the narrator or speaker of a text.
4.B Identify and explain the function of point of view in a narrative.
7.A Develop a paragraph that includes 1) a claim that requires defense with evidence from the text and 2) the evidence itself.
